title: Caponata
subtitle: sicilian sweet and sour aubergine
excerpt: Caponata is a Sicilian sweet and sour vegetable dish built on fried aubergine, celery, olives, and capers in a thick agrodolce sauce. It is served at room temperature as an antipasto or side dish and improves significantly when made a day ahead. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Caponata is one of the most recognisable dishes of Sicilian cooking. Arab influence brought the sweet and sour flavour combination to the island during the medieval period. Every Sicilian family has their own version, and debates about the correct recipe are fierce.

recipe.batchNotes: Caponata keeps well in the fridge for up to 4 days. Make a double batch easily.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made at least 1 hour ahead and ideally overnight. The flavour improves as it sits.

content.text: balance . the ratio of white wine vinegar to sugar that gives the sauce its sweet-sharp character. The technique is to fry the aubergine separately in hot oil until deeply golden, then build the sauce in a separate pan and combine everything at the end. This recipe serves 4.
Made a day ahead and left at room temperature, caponata is significantly better than when freshly made. The flavours mellow and the aubergine soaks up the sauce.

Heat 6 tablespoons of olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Fry the aubergine cubes in batches without overcrowding, turning occasionally, until deep golden on all sides, about 8 minutes per batch. Remove and set aside.
In a large saucepan, heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook for 8 minutes until the onion is soft and the celery is slightly tender.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Add the capers, olives, and raisins. Stir to combine.
Pour in the white wine vinegar, sprinkle in the granulated sugar, and stir well. Taste the sauce . it should be clearly both sweet and sour. Adjust with more vinegar or sugar if needed.

Add the fried aubergine and pine nuts to the pan and stir gently to combine. Cook together for 5 minutes over low heat. Remove from the heat, leave to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

attrs.problem: Aubergine soaking up all the oil
attrs.solution: This is normal and unavoidable. Use the full amount of oil specified and fry in hot oil - the aubergine will release some back into the pan as it cooks.

attrs.problem: Sauce tastes flat or too sharp
attrs.solution: Add more sugar a half-teaspoon at a time, tasting as you go. The balance should be clearly agrodolce - both the vinegar and sweetness should be detectable but neither overwhelming.

attrs.problem: Aubergine is mushy in the final dish
attrs.solution: The pieces were too small or cooked too long in the sauce. Cut the aubergine into larger chunks and only add it to the sauce at the very end, cooking together for no more than 5 minutes.

content.text: Caponata is from Sicily and is one of the island's most famous dishes. Every family has their own recipe. Some add pine nuts and raisins; others leave them out. Some add cocoa powder or chocolate in the Palermo style. The sweet and sour combination came to Sicily from Arab traders during the medieval period. It is a dish that has been evolving for over a thousand years.
